positioning: For tactile coffee drinkers and quiet collectors, Maren Solis is the small-batch ceramic and woodblock studio that pairs raw wood-ash stoneware with open process notes.
values: Honest raw clay and visible kiln marks
Small-batch utility built for daily rituals
Open studio notes over gatekept craft

audience_segments.who: Home brewers and ritual-minded tea and coffee drinkers
audience_segments.wants: Durable stoneware cups and drippers that feel grounded in the hand
Numbered woodblock kiln studies and one-off sculptural vessels with firing stories

dynamic.label: maker→collector
evidence: voice_1: shares kiln unloading temperatures and glaze failures openly
voice_2: signs every firing note by hand and invites collectors into glaze choices

strategy: Newcomers enter through affordable studio paper pieces or a single stoneware espresso cup, then deepen into daily pour-over tools and open throwing notes. Repeat fans graduate to numbered woodblock kiln prints, one-off basalt vessels, and custom table commissions.

do: Name the clay body, glaze mineral, or firing step
Speak in short, warm studio sentences
Invite visitors to notice weight, rim, and surface
dont: Use hype, countdowns, or luxury cliches
Invent awards, reviews, or unverified claims
Over-explain when two calm lines are enough
samples: Pulled from cone 10 reduction this morning—warm iron speckles along every rim.
This cup holds four ounces and keeps heat long after the crema settles.
Every print starts as ash rubbed from the kiln shelf onto Japanese kozo paper.

visual.lighting_mood: Warm north-window daylight softened by focused gallery pools

story_beats.beat: From raw clay, wood ash, and firing logs to finished stoneware
Daily coffee and table rituals shaped on the wheel
Numbered woodblock kiln prints and one-off basalt vessels

claims.claim: Stoneware pieces are wheel-thrown and fired to cone 10 reduction
Glaze tests incorporate sifted hardwood ash from studio firings
Woodblock prints document the kiln shelf patterns after each firing
